fatal_errors: The proposed comparison omits the governing intervention: aging the same SLM alloy at 750°C for 50 h to create L12/L21 precipitates and comparing it with the as-printed state.
The baseline is changed to unspecified conventional alloys, so composition and processing are not controlled and oxidation differences cannot be attributed to precipitation.
The hypothesis does not predict the observed higher mass gain of the aged state or connect it to Cr-depleted precipitates and precipitate–matrix interfaces.
It misses formation of the continuous Cr2O3 transport barrier, the key mediator in the target mechanism.
The stated oxygen-pressure range is unsupported by the target study, whose oxidation atmosphere was not explicitly specified.
explanation: The response addresses high-temperature oxidation of multiprincipal-element alloys and offers a broadly plausible thermodynamic account involving elemental reactivity, atomic size, redox potential, and oxide-film evolution. The cited studies support that general framework for CoCrFeNiMn-type alloys, but they do not establish the specific behavior of the SLM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy or its aging-induced precipitates. The reconstruction fails to isolate the target variable, namely as-printed versus directly aged material of identical composition. It consequently misses the central finding that aging produces Cr-depleted L12/L21 precipitates and added interfaces, delaying protective Cr2O3 formation and increasing mass gain while leaving activation energies broadly similar. The proposed measurements are relevant but the falsification rule is qualitative and does not distinguish this mechanism from competing transport- or microstructure-controlled explanations. The 600–900°C range overlaps only part of the target range and excludes the 1050–1200°C regime where inner Al/Ti-rich oxidation becomes important.
